title: Passes for a college fest that sells out in minutes
summary: Sell a fixed number of passes fairly when thousands of students press Buy at the same moment.
context: Tunga Tickets sells passes for college fests. A headline night has 8,000 passes, and 60,000 students arrive when sales open at 18:00. Each student may buy four. Payment takes about a minute, and many never finish.
At the last fest, 300 extra passes were sold and refunds took a week. Scripts also bought hundreds of passes and resold them outside the gate.
must_handle: Never more passes are sold than exist.
A pass held for an unfinished payment returns to sale after a while.
A student sees a clear answer quickly, even when they cannot get a pass.
One person cannot beat the limit with several tabs or a script.
The rest of the site stays up for other events during the rush.
show_in_answer: How a pass is held, paid for and released.
How the opening rush is shaped before it reaches the database.
What a student sees at each stage.
How you would test this before the real evening.
